title: To restrain oneself and return to ritual is benevolence
subtitle: Analects 12.1
timeLabel: Pre-Qin sayings tradition · interpreted through Sui–Tang classical learning
shortSummary: The line connects self-regulation, ritual and benevolence, opening a path into the relationship between Confucian cultivation and social order.
curatorialDescription: Ritual is not only ceremonial surface; it also concerns relationship, role, measure and shared order. Restraining oneself should not be reduced to suppressing individuality, but read within the problem of benevolence.
Ritual can enter education and politics as an institution while also shaping everyday conduct and self-cultivation. These dimensions are connected but not interchangeable.
Sui–Tang classical learning brought earlier texts into new commentarial and educational systems. The passage therefore links the Analects with a Tang institutional context.
researchNote: The first release uses the received section locator Analects 12.1. The modern Chinese explanation and English translation are original museum summaries.

quote.original: 克己復禮為仁。一日克己復禮，天下歸仁焉。
quote.interpretation: Restraining the tendency to centre only one's own desires and returning to ritual relations is one way benevolence is practised.
